description: The screw thread itself is physically damaged, preventing proper engagement during tightening.
An unexpected object such as a washer is present in the assembly location, altering contact geometry.
The robot attempts tightening but no screw is present, often due to pick failure or skipped step.
The threaded hole in the plate is damaged, preventing proper screw engagement.
Robot is performing a screw loosening operation rather than tightening. This is a normal operational phase but may appear anomalous if only tightening behavior is expected.
Increased mechanical friction at one robot axis joint or gearbox, requiring higher motor torque to maintain the commanded trajectory. Simulates dirt or age-related gear wear.
The motor commutation phase is deliberately offset in firmware, reducing torque-forming efficiency without affecting the commanded path or velocity. Simulates electrical or magnetic component wear.
The vacuum gripper fails to activate and never picks up the can. The robot completes the motion but carries no payload.
The vacuum gripper releases the can mid-trajectory at a random point during transport, causing an abrupt loss of payload load on the robot arm.
A physical weight is attached to one robot axis, increasing its effective inertia and gravity loading. Affects torque demands on all joints due to the kinematic chain.

The robot unexpectedly collides with an object in its workspace during motion. Collision objects include foam cubes, hanging cables, or cardboard cartons placed at random positions. Impacts range from head-on strikes to glancing contacts and may also occur when the previously hit object swings back.
The can being transported has an unexpected weight that deviates from the nominal 241 g. This may simulate a damaged can or upstream filling errors. Tested weights range from 41 g (empty) to 448 g.
A cable is attached along the robot arm with cable ties, introducing pose-dependent friction and gravity loading on affected axes as the cable bends and twists during motion.

The can is detected at an unusual position outside the normal distribution, causing the robot to approach from an atypical joint configuration. This indicates an upstream process fault such as a worn conveyor belt.

The robot's mounting platform is unstable due to released wheel brakes or uneven foam placement beneath it, introducing low-frequency vibrations into the arm during motion. Conceptually related to fixture_instability (fault_id 11) but applies to the robot base rather than the workpiece.
